title: Single-Electrode, Bidirectional Control of Heart Rate via Vagus Nerve Modulation
author: Shane Bender
materials: Stimulating/blocking source: open-source COSMIIC project's GAMMA module
Controller Software: Windows PC with LabVIEW 2024
Replacement software should follow a similar data flow: ECG acquisition → Heart Rate Calculation → Fuzzy Logic Controller → Output to current source
Expose the vagus on each side
Isolate the system and remove tonic activity
Calibrate stimulation slope for the control (distal) electrode
Enter these calibration values into the controller
Begin recording data for each trial
Stimulating/blocking source: open-source COSMIIC project's GAMMA module

steps.title: Prepare Animal and Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia in male Sprague-Dawley rats (7–11 weeks old, 400–600 g) and prepare the surgical site.

substeps.instruction: Place rat in induction chamber and deliver 3-5% isoflurane for 2-5 minutes until unconscious.
Weigh the rat and place it in an anesthesia nose cone on a heated pad.
While maintaining 3-5% isoflurane, shave the ventral cervical neck over the trachea.
Monitor vital signs until appropriate anesthesia depth for intubation is reached (minimum breathing rate: 20 breaths/min; minimum heart rate: 200 beats/min).
Ensure sufficient sedation to maintain unconsciousness without isoflurane for approximately 1-2 minutes during intubation.

steps.title: Perform Tracheal Intubation
steps.instruction: Intubate the rat to provide mechanical ventilation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare an intubation board, large forceps, laryngoscope, and a 14-gauge (or 16-gauge) angiocatheter.
Remove rat from nose cone, place on intubation board, and secure the nose/upper jaw.
Grasp the tongue with large forceps and use the laryngoscope to visualize the larynx.
Insert the angiocatheter into the trachea.
Connect the angiocatheter to a ventilator and begin ventilation at 4-5 mL stroke volume and 60 breaths per minute.
Transfer the rat back to the heated pad in a supine position, ensuring the angiocatheter is not pulled.

steps.title: Isolate Vagus Nerve and Place Electrodes
steps.instruction: Surgically expose the vagus nerves and install the stimulation electrodes.

substeps.instruction: Make two rostral-caudal incisions in the skin on each side of the trachea over the vagus nerves, connecting them to form an 'H' shape.
Blunt dissect to isolate the vagus nerves (typically bundled with the carotid artery and jugular vein).
Place two custom-fabricated bipolar platinum cuff electrodes (1x1 mm windows) on the right vagus nerve, ensuring no kinking or pulling of the nerve.
Use fine forceps to crush the right side nerve proximal to the electrodes to keep the nerve structurally intact.
Optionally crush or completely cut the left vagus nerve.

steps.title: Calibrate Control Electrode
steps.instruction: Determine the stimulation parameters for the distal (control) electrode.

substeps.instruction: Find a stimulation amplitude that elicits maximal heart rate decrease (test at 30 Hz, 50 μs per phase; expected currents 0.1 mA to 5 mA peak-to-peak).
If AV block occurs (heart rate drops suddenly by roughly half), reduce amplitude until normal conduction resumes.
Record baseline heart rate without stimulation.
Increase control electrode stimulation in steps of 1 Hz and plot the heart rate change.
Fit a linear regression to the data to obtain the slope in bpm/Hz.

steps.title: Calibrate Perturbation Electrode
steps.instruction: Determine the maximal stimulation amplitude for the proximal (perturbation) electrode.

substeps.instruction: Using the same procedure as the control electrode, find the maximal stimulation amplitude at 30 Hz and 50 μs per phase.

steps.title: Calibrate Blocking Waveform
steps.instruction: Determine the block start and slope for the control electrode.

substeps.instruction: Apply maximal stimulation to the perturbation electrode to elicit bradycardia.
Increase the amplitude of a 10 kHz square wave blocking waveform on the control electrode until the heart rate begins to increase toward baseline; record this as the block starting current.
Continue increasing the block amplitude and plot the resultant heart rate.
Once heart rate reaches the pre-perturbation baseline, fit a line to the data and record the blocking slope in bpm/mA.

steps.title: Set Controller Parameters
steps.instruction: Establish the setpoint and baseline for the bidirectional controller.

substeps.instruction: Briefly apply 30 Hz stimulation to the control electrode for ~30 seconds.
Compare the stimulation bradycardia heart rate (0%) and the post-stimulation baseline heart rate (100%).
Set the controller setpoint halfway between these values (50%).
Record baseline heart rate for at least 2 minutes before activating the controller.

steps.title: Execute Control Trial
steps.instruction: Run the heart rate control experiment across different gain settings.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the controller and allow it to bring the heart rate down to the 50% setpoint for 2 minutes.
Set the desired controller Gain (2x, 5x, or 10x).
Ramp the stimulation frequency on the perturbation electrode up to 30 Hz over 5 minutes, then ramp back down to 1 Hz over 5 minutes.
Allow the controller to run for an additional 2 minutes after the perturbation ramp.
Turn off the controller and allow the heart rate to return to baseline.
Repeat the entire trial process for the other two gain values.

steps.title: Euthanize Animal
steps.instruction: Perform euthanasia according to institutional guidelines.

substeps.instruction: Increase anesthesia to 5%.
Inject sodium pentobarbital into the heart using a 22-gauge needle (or use an approved institutional method).
